data.one_liner: Send real-time 16-bit PCM audio to device speakers from Flutter.
data.what_it_does: It streams real-time PCM audio (16-bit integer) directly to device speakers using a low-frequency, event-based callback mechanism. It is designed for applications that generate audio on the fly, such as software synthesizers or custom audio generators.
use_when: You are building an app that generates audio in real-time (e.g., soundfonts, synthesizers).
You want a low-dependency solution to stream raw PCM audio frames to device speakers.
avoid_when: You just want to play pre-recorded audio files like MP3s or WAVs.
You need a high-level music player or streaming framework.
strengths: Zero dependencies besides Flutter and the host platform.
Event-based feeding integrates well with the Flutter event loop.
Cross-platform support for Android, iOS, and macOS.
weaknesses: Not designed for playback of standard audio files.
Requires manual sample generation and buffer management.
data.setup_notes: Enable required platforms in your Flutter project configuration.

alternatives.name: audioplayers
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick audioplayers if you need to play pre-recorded audio files or URLs rather than streaming raw PCM data.

alternatives.name: just_audio
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick just_audio for feature-rich audio playback of files, playlists, and streams.
